items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: Duke and I are great friends.

ctx.x: What about Duke Ellington? You know him personally?

Well sure. Duke and I are great friends. How'd that happen? Well, through Bonnie. Through Bonnie Biggore, my cousin. When they booked the tour in Texas, I wired Bonnie that I was there and I wanted them to be my guests at my house. So I met them in Austin, Texas, which is 75 miles from San Antonio and then I brought them into San Antonio. By the same token, cab the same way. In those days they had what they called the circuit where they played all of these theater dates. That's most of the dates that Ellington…
When did they have that flood there?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: We got so popular that Duke Ellington was playing there at the Pilgrim Temple. We were playing down there for Don Robie... We closed Duke up.

ctx.x: Yes, we had a job off of us. We didn't know whether we were good enough for it or not because we only knew how to play three songs. What, do you remember what the three were? I Love You, The Sheik of Arabi were two of them. I can't remember the third one. But anyhow, after we got to Dallas, then there was a band traveling with me on the same train. It was the year that the New Orleans Pelicans were playing Wichita Falls in the Classic. And the fellas in this band, the T&T band, with some great musicians, later on…
I remember seeing a picture of Duke Ellington wearing pants like that.

Well this was the style in those days. And this whole outfit was made by one of the best tailors in Dallas through one of the bookers, the man that found me, Bernard Goldberg. This other picture you see here is later on when I had stopped playing I was only featuring myself on two or three numbers. I had to take care of the business of the band. This was taken in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. And naturally this one here that you're looking at I was eight years old. This is in my backyard. You notice the wash tubs?…

items.title: Don Albert and Herbert Hall Interview, 1978-08-03
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Well at that time we all were listening. Oh yeah. We all were listening to Duke Youngstown.

ctx.x: Did you listen to any other baritones?
Well at that time we all were listening. Oh yeah. We all were listening to Duke Youngstown.
